answer: The protocol validates 1,000 distinct service slots through capacity-reservations, where each agent must secure a fixed-size buffer on verified hardware. A verifier probes these sectors to ensure they do not whisper through shared relays, demanding a direct connection that forces each node to wander across assigned geographical sub-segments. This architecture treats data like compressed shale, where any compression or signal overlap triggers a permanent deposit slash. An honest participant pays 1x cost, whereas an attacker pays 1,000x for isolated, non-pooled slots, with fees held for 90 days.
